candidate:
REWARD_MACHINE:
STATES: u0, u1
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u0
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, has_door_key) -> u1
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, door_open) -> u0
(u1, else) -> u1
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, has_door_key, u1) -> 0.1
(u1, door_open, u0) -> 1.0
feedback: Accepted. The two-state cyclic RM is a faithful, minimal encoding of the recurring gift->answer loop. u0 (no key held; every gift so far answered) and u1 (key held; gift pending) are entered/exited only via the two propositions: (u0, has_door_key)->u1 marks the key landing and (u1, door_open)->u0 marks the answer, which matches the environment guarantees that door_open can only follow has_door_key and that the two never co-occur. Both states carry else self-loops, so all irrelevant happenings (turning/moving, the 10-step door_open dwell after an answer, the door shutting again, truncation) are absorbed without spurious rewards; in particular, because the machine returns to u0 at the opening step, the 1.0 fires once per answer rather than once per open step, so there is no reward farming during the door-open dwell. The 1.0 on (u1, door_open, u0) equals the environment's per-gift payoff exactly, and the 0.1 on (u0, has_door_key, u1) is a small, bounded progress marker that cannot be farmed (keys arrive only with empty hands and a shut door, so the bonus actually rewards fast answering and higher gift throughput) and does not distort the optimal policy. No regression transitions are needed: the key cannot be dropped or lost, the only exit from u1 is a successful open, and an unanswered key at truncation correctly leaves the machine in u1 with no terminal reward. Ordered transition coverage is complete for the only possible event order (has_door_key then door_open); the reverse order is impossible per the constraints. FINAL_STATES: u0 is declared and accepting — u0 is precisely the condition that every key received so far has been answered, the acceptance condition of this cyclic maintenance task. Labels are predicate-only (no action or env event names), and the block format with (state, label) transitions and (state, label, next-state) reward triples matches the paper format. Minor note only: the 0.1 fires on an agent-uncontrollable event, but it is harmless and bounded; setting it to 0 would not change correctness.
